why:
This part completes your first-reply coverage after 1.e4. It covers the Scandinavian, Alekhine, Pirc, Modern and Nimzowitsch, plus short responses to eleven unusual first moves. The Vienna, Grand Prix and Advance tabs still cover their own defences.

The shared principle is to develop and support the centre, not to force one setup against every reply. In the Scandinavian you first capture on d5; against the Alekhine you gain space with e5. Against the Pirc, Modern and Nimzowitsch you occupy d4, but must still watch concrete central challenges.

The unusual replies are grouped for navigation, not because they all lead to the same position. Follow their shown continuations and check threats. These are practical starting lines, not exhaustive coverage of every later move.

variations.middlegame: Capture on d5, then develop. A queen recapture allows Nc3 with tempo, while the knight reply needs its own continuation. Do not chase the queen at the expense of development.
